thread:
maria: :rotating_light: getting reports of TLS handshake failures from customers hitting api.redwood-inference.com around 13:14 UTC. Errors show as TLS alert (handshake_failure) and connection resets coming from Cloudflare edge IPs. Observability shows spike in 524/523-like symptoms at the edge.
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 -> oncall: aj (15:00). Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident-1742009876.
pagerduty: PagerDuty notification sent to @aj.
aj: I can reproduce from my laptop — `curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health` times out with TLS handshake errors when routed via Cloudflare. Hitting origin LB IP directly (bypass CF) returns 200.
maria: that suggests Cloudflare edge TLS or routing issue, not our origin. Good to confirm origin healthy.
sasha: checking edge metrics — Cloudflare upstream responses are showing elevated `525` and `524` over last 10m for US-EAST and EU-WEST. Also seeing `ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR` from browser-side reports.
kevin: customer impact: at least three major customers reporting API calls failing intermittently; one support ticket flagged as Sev2. Will escalate if it persists.
aj: attempted `dig api.redwood-inference.com @1.1.1.1` — resolves to Cloudflare IPs as expected. Traceroute shows early reset at Cloudflare nodes.
maria: can we quickly verify whether Cloudflare turned on any new TLS setting or global change? I'm opening a support ticket. Ticket ID: CF-112233 (submitted).
sasha: I can flip Cloudflare proxy to DNS-only for api.redwood-inference.com (turn orange cloud -> grey) to force traffic to our LB. TTLs low but still some cached edges. This will bypass Cloudflare features but should restore handshakes quickly for most clients. Thoughts?
aj: +1 for DNS-only rollback. Need ops approval to change prod DNS. Also plan a runbook step: 1) set DNS to DNS-only 2) monitor 3) revert when CF confirms fix.
kevin: notify sales/CS to hold customer calls, mention rollback plan and ETA ~10-20m.
maria: I'll own the DNS change. Preparing console steps now.
incident-bot: action assigned -> maria: perform dns toggle (CF console) and post confirmation.
maria: doing the toggle now. Command snippet for internal record:
```
// Cloudflare console manual steps
DNS -> select api.redwood-inference.com -> toggle Proxy status to OFF (DNS only)
```
maria: toggled to DNS-only at 13:28 UTC. Propagating.
aj: verifying — curl to api.example (still hitting CF cached nodes) but direct `curl --resolve api.redwood-inference.com:443:203.0.113.10 https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health` to LB IP returns 200.
sasha: CDN edges are gradually serving new DNS; we're seeing handshake errors decrease in real-time metrics. 13:31 UTC counts dropping from 120/s to 12/s.
kevin: posting status update to customers: "We've identified a Cloudflare edge TLS issue affecting some requests. We have temporarily disabled Cloudflare proxying for api.redwood-inference.com to restore service. Some clients may experience residual DNS caching. We're monitoring and will update."
aj: contacted Cloudflare support with ticket CF-112233 and included pcap + logs. Support replied acknowledging an incident on their edge and routing team is investigating. They recommended DNS change as a mitigation.
maria: rolling monitoring checklists: checking auth provider (ok), metrics ingestion (ok), no increased error rate at origin.
sasha: runbook note: add short term rule to route traffic away from CF for any future TLS anomalies (config flag: `edge_bypass_on_tls_errors`). Filed infra task: INF-789.
kevin: handoff in 40m — I'll stay until 14:30 UTC then hand off to sasha for follow-up and postmortem.
aj: temporary mitigation looks stable. Still seeing occasional clients that hit older CF caches -> those will clear within TTL (~60s) or via cache purge.
maria: Cloudflare support updated ticket: "We observed transient TLS handshakes failures caused by SNI mismatch on some edges; rollback initiated and mitigation deployed." They said they will notify when fully resolved. Ticket CF-112233 -> updated 13:45 UTC.
incident-bot: Severity reduced to P2 based on mitigations.
kevin: prepping incident summary to share in #incidents and SOC: timeline, mitigation (DNS toggle), CF ticket, affected customers, next steps.
sasha: action items: 1) autopilot rule to automatically disable CF proxy for api when 5xx/TLS thresholds reached; 2) add health check that verifies TLS handshake at CF layer; 3) coordinate with CF for a postmortem.
maria: adding task: CF postmortem request + internal postmortem schedule.
aj: leaving notes in runbook, will include exact curl/tcpdump commands used.
kevin: handing off to sasha now — I'll be available if anything regresses. sasha, you're on point from 14:30 UTC. :thumbsup:
sasha: acknowledged, taking over. I'll complete the incident ticket and lead the follow-up.
incident-bot: Incident marked "mitigated" at 14:02 UTC. Follow-up tasks: INF-789, PM-452 (postmortem), CS-998 (customer comms).
maria: Thanks team. Postmortem will include timeline, why CF change was required, decision rationale for DNS toggle vs. traffic shift, and a plan to reduce blast radius in future.
kevin: I'll draft the customer-facing note for affected accounts and link it in the postmortem.
aj: recommend adding synthetic monitors that perform full TLS handshake via CF edges from multiple regions. Filing MON-321.
sasha: closing bridge. We'll reconvene tomorrow 10:00 UTC for postmortem sync.
support-bot: Logged incident 1742009876 -> severity P1 -> status mitigated -> followups assigned.
maria: final note: no evidence of origin compromise, root cause appears to be Cloudflare edge TLS glitch. Keep CF ticket linked for full root cause.
